output_evals.name: scheme_choice_free
output_evals.prompt: My ICP canister needs to sign attestations that only my own off-chain service will verify. Which threshold signature scheme and management canister method should I use? Two or three sentences, no code.
expected_behaviors: Recommends Ed25519 (threshold Schnorr with algorithm ed25519)
Justifies it with the best threshold-signing throughput on ICP (and/or simplicity), since the verifier imposes no scheme
Names `sign_with_schnorr` (and optionally `schnorr_public_key`) rather than `sign_with_ecdsa`

output_evals.name: scheme_choice_verifier
output_evals.prompt: For each of these, which ICP threshold signature scheme (key_id) should my canister use: (a) an Ethereum transaction, (b) a Bitcoin Taproot key-path spend, (c) a JWT with alg ES256, (d) a Solana transfer? One line each.
expected_behaviors: (a) ECDSA with curve secp256k1
(b) Schnorr with algorithm bip340secp256k1, mentioning the bip341 aux (empty merkle root for key-path-only outputs)
(c) ECDSA with curve secp256r1 (P-256)
(d) Schnorr with algorithm ed25519

output_evals.name: throughput_design
output_evals.prompt: I want my canister to issue a fresh threshold-signed receipt for every one of ~500 user actions per second. Will that work on ICP? Answer in one short paragraph with the design you'd use instead.
expected_behaviors: States that signing throughput is roughly 10 signatures per second per key (shared with other canisters using the key), with only somewhat higher short bursts
Says 500 signatures/s is not feasible and requests beyond capacity get rejected with a 'request queue ... is full' error
Proposes batching (one signature over a Merkle root / hash of many receipts), queueing with a timer and backoff, or not signing per action
Optionally suggests Ed25519 for best throughput or certified data / canister signatures when only ICP verifies

output_evals.name: rust_sign_ed25519
output_evals.prompt: Write just the Rust update method (ic-cdk 0.20) that signs a message with threshold Ed25519 using a per-caller derivation path and returns the 64-byte signature. Include the use statements. No Cargo.toml, no explanation.
expected_behaviors: Imports from `ic_cdk_management_canister` (NOT `ic_cdk::management_canister`, which ic-cdk 0.20 no longer has)
Uses `SignWithSchnorrArgs` with `SchnorrKeyId { algorithm: SchnorrAlgorithm::Ed25519, name }` and `aux: None`
Passes the message itself, not a hash of it
Builds the derivation path from `msg_caller()`, not from a caller-supplied argument
Does not hardcode cycles: relies on the helper attaching the fee

output_evals.name: ecdsa_message_hash
output_evals.prompt: My canister calls sign_with_ecdsa with message_hash set to the UTF-8 bytes of a 200-character string and the call is rejected. What's wrong and how do I fix it? Short answer.
expected_behaviors: Explains `message_hash` must be exactly 32 bytes
Says to hash the message first with the hash the verifier expects (SHA-256, Keccak-256 for Ethereum, the Bitcoin sighash)
Does not suggest truncating or padding the message

output_evals.name: derive_with_chain_code
output_evals.prompt: In my Rust canister I fetch ecdsa_public_key once with an empty derivation path and want to compute child keys locally with ic-secp256k1. Show just the derivation function.
expected_behaviors: Keeps the `chain_code` returned by `ecdsa_public_key`
Uses `derive_subkey_with_chain_code(&path, &chain_code)`
Warns that `derive_subkey` (zero chain code) gives the wrong key for a non-master key

output_evals.name: fees_and_key_names
output_evals.prompt: What key names exist for threshold signing on ICP, which work locally with icp-cli, and how many cycles does one signature cost? Keep it to a short list.
expected_behaviors: key_1 = production, 26_153_846_153 cycles per signature
test_key_1 = testing, 10_000_000_000 cycles per signature, not for anything of value
Both (and dfx_test_key) are available on the icp-cli local network, whose master keys differ from mainnet so local addresses differ
States that public key calls (ecdsa_public_key, schnorr_public_key) are free; only signing is charged

output_evals.name: ethereum_recovery_id
output_evals.prompt: sign_with_ecdsa gave me a 64-byte signature but my Ethereum transaction needs v / y_parity. How do I get it? Two or three sentences.
expected_behaviors: States the IC returns r||s without a recovery id
Computes y_parity by trial recovery against the known public key and the 32-byte Keccak-256 digest (e.g. ic-secp256k1 `try_recovery_from_digest`)
Does not claim the IC can return v directly

trigger_evals.description: Queries testing whether the threshold-signatures skill activates. should_trigger should load it; should_not_trigger should route elsewhere (vetkeys, cketh, evm-rpc, user-sign-in).
should_trigger: Give my canister its own Bitcoin address and let it sign transactions
How do I sign a Solana transaction from a Rust canister?
Issue ES256 JWTs from my ICP backend that a normal JWT library can verify
sign_with_ecdsa keeps failing with 'request queue for key is full'
Which signature scheme should my canister use, ECDSA or Ed25519?
Derive an Ethereum address for each user of my canister
should_not_trigger: Encrypt a message so only a given principal can decrypt it
Let users deposit USDC and get ckUSDC in my app
Read the latest Ethereum block number from a canister
Add Internet Identity login to my frontend
